title: Understanding the Nature of Solutions
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: The periodic nature of trigonometric functions means that solutions repeat at regular intervals.

content.text: Sine and cosine repeat every 2π radians, while tangent repeats every π radians.
A restricted interval asks for only the solutions inside a specified range. A general solution describes all solutions.

examples.question: If x = π/6 is a solution of sin(x) = 1/2, give another solution.
examples.solution: Because sine has period 2π, x = π/6 + 2π is also a solution.

key_ideas: General solutions describe infinitely many solutions.
Restricted intervals limit which solutions are accepted.
misconceptions: Assuming the inverse trigonometric function gives every solution.
Forgetting the period when generating additional solutions.
